ops.title: skip_permissions cold-path thread leak (known residual)
ops.body:
v9.20.0 (ce8b4f32) removed `_SKIP_CACHE` so daemon-bound requests walk the client's process tree fresh per call — resumed sessions with changed launch flags no longer get stale consent. Codex security review (gpt-5.6-sol xhigh, 2026-07-16) confirmed the fix and flagged one **pre-existing residual it does not close**:

A hook-created thread does not inherit the request ContextVar, so a first read of `evt.skip_permissions` from inside a user-spawned thread (e.g. `ThreadPoolExecutor`) sees `reqenv.current() is None` and falls into `_cold_skip_permissions()` — a `functools.cache` that, inside the resident daemon process, memoizes the **daemon's own ancestry** for the daemon's lifetime. Failure shape: a bypass-launched session starts the daemon and a threaded hook primes the cache `True`; a later non-bypass session's threaded hook reads stale `True`. This path predates the `_SKIP_CACHE` removal and requires the unusual offload-first-property-read-to-a-thread pattern; normal same-thread dispatch constructs a fresh event inside `request_scope` and is unaffected.

Secondary accepted risk from the same review: per-request walks mean pathological `ps` timeouts (5s each) can serialize past the daemon client's 30s fail-open deadline under heavy same-session concurrency.

If fixing: the cold path should not be reachable (or not process-cached) inside the daemon process; binding the walk result into the event at construction defeats the deliberate laziness, so prefer making `_cold_skip_permissions` daemon-aware or propagating the request context to hook-spawned threads.
